title: We’re covering $1 million in security scans and fixes through November 8, 2026
text: **Update:** The original $1M Deep Scan campaign has ended. Run your first deep scan for free. First-time users of CodeRabbit Secure with 2+ subscription seats in their organization get up to $1,000 in credits towards their first Deep Scan. [Run Free Deep Scan](https://app.coderabbit.ai/security). The original campaign offered up to $5,000 in Deep Scan usage for any organization with two or more members, including open-source projects, current and former customers, and organizations that had never used CodeRabbit. We put up to $1 million behind it on a first-come, first-served basis while the allocation lasted. CodeRabbit is now part of the OpenAI Daybreak Defense Network. CodeRabbit Secure uses GPT 6.1 Sol and GPT Cyber models to help teams find and fix security vulnerabilities. Deep Scan examines your codebase and independently verifies which vulnerabilities are exploitable, and helps you fix them before hackers get to them. CodeRabbit Secure has found broken access controls and authentication failures and can help your team fix them. The original offer was scheduled to run through November 8, 2026, with up to $5,000 in covered usage per eligible organization (with 2+ members in the org) while the $1 million allocation lasted. ## Look beyond the latest change Deep Scan examines committed code across an entire repository. It maps the codebase in detail, hunts for vulnerabilities across its code paths, examines the safeguards already in place, and uses semantic analysis to assess whether a vulnerability can actually be exploited. Before a finding reaches your team, an independent verifier reopens the code and rejects anything the evidence doesn't support. Each published finding includes supporting evidence and an assessment of its reachability and exploitability. Your team gets the context it needs to understand the issue and decide what deserves attention first. Keep the security tools already in your stack running. Deep Scan works alongside them, adding reasoning about first-party application logic and risks that become visible only when code is read in context. If a path crosses linked repositories, Deep Scan can use that context too. For eligible findings, CodeRabbit can draft a fix that follows the standards already used in the codebase. A developer reviews the proposed change and remains responsible for what ships. ## Why we're covering the scans Developers are not the only people using AI to make sense of unfamiliar code. The same capability can help attackers search mature codebases for paths no one has followed in years. Teams need enough defensive capacity to examine their own code just as closely. Open-source projects are a big part of why we're doing this. Companies rely on open-source software that is often maintained by small teams without dedicated security staff. A vulnerability in one widely used project can affect every organization that relies on it. We want those maintainers to see what Deep Scan finds without budget being the reason they have to wait. ## Put Deep Scan to work Run your first deep scan for free. First-time users of CodeRabbit Secure with 2+ subscription seats in their organization get up to $1,000 in credits towards their first Deep Scan. Sign in or create an account, connect a repository, and run Deep Scan. Start with the repository your team or your community depends on most.
